questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes cyclic vs negacyclic convolution for polynomials of length n?
options: Cyclic uses x^n = -1; negacyclic uses x^n = 1
Cyclic uses x^n = 1; negacyclic uses x^n = -1
Cyclic and negacyclic are the same; the names are historical
Negacyclic only exists when q is composite
questions.explanation: Cyclic convolution corresponds to reduction modulo x^n − 1 (so x^n = 1). Negacyclic convolution corresponds to reduction modulo x^n + 1 (so x^n = −1).

questions.question: In the “twisted NTT” method for multiplying in Z_q[y]/(y^n + 1), what condition must the twist element psi satisfy (at minimum)?
options: psi must be a generator of Z_q as an additive group
questions.explanation: To turn negacyclic convolution into cyclic convolution via a twist, you need psi^n = −1, which implies psi has order 2n in the multiplicative group.

questions.question: Working modulo x^8 + 1, what is x^9 reduced to?
questions.explanation: Modulo x^8 + 1 we have x^8 = −1, so x^9 = x·x^8 = −x.

questions.question: In the twisted NTT setup with psi of order 2n, the n-th root omega used by the cyclic NTT is:
questions.explanation: If psi has order 2n, then omega = psi^2 has order n and can be used as the primitive n-th root for the cyclic NTT.

questions.question: With the even/odd split a(x) = a_e(y) + x·a_o(y) and b(x) = b_e(y) + x·b_o(y) where y = x^2, what is the coefficient of x in the product a(x)·b(x)?
questions.explanation: Multiply out (a_e + x a_o)(b_e + x b_o) = (a_e b_e + x^2 a_o b_o) + x(a_e b_o + a_o b_e). The x term is a_e b_o + a_o b_e.

questions.question: Kyber-style coefficient compression maps c in [0,q) to t in [0,2^d). Which expression matches that intent?
questions.explanation: Compression is a quantization step: scale by 2^d/q and round to the nearest integer so t fits in d bits while approximating c.

questions.question: In the pack_bits implementation used in this lesson, where do the bits of the first value go?
options: Into the most-significant bits of the first byte
Into the least-significant bits of the first byte
They are stored as a separate length-prefixed field before the bytes
They are dropped; only the second value is packed
questions.explanation: The code builds an accumulator by shifting the next value in at the current low-bit position, then emits bytes from the low end. That places the first value in the least-significant bits of the first output byte.

questions.question: A production ML-KEM implementation must not branch early on mismatch during ciphertext checks (e.g., comparing recomputed ciphertext or decompress/pack results). Why?
options: Because branching makes the code longer, which hurts performance
Because it can leak information via timing/power/cache, acting like a decryption-validity oracle
Because the standard forbids using if-statements in cryptographic code
Because compression only works when executed on a GPU
questions.explanation: Early exits and data-dependent branches can leak whether a ciphertext was valid via timing or microarchitectural signals, which attackers can amplify into an oracle.
